text:
I am not one of those who abandoned the land

to the mercy of enemies.

Their flatteries leave me cold,

my songs are not for them to praise.


But I pity the exiles.

Like that of a deserter, like that of one half-dead,

dark is your road, wanderer;

bitterness infects your foreign bread.


But here, in the half-light of the conflagration,

when hardly one friend remains to know,

we survivors do not give way

before anything, before a single blow.


Surely the reckoning will be made

after this cloud passes,

we are people without tears,

straighter than you... prouder.




1922

translation.title: I Am Not One of Those Who Abandoned the Land
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the contrast between exile and remaining inside catastrophe.
